findings.source_quote: The residents of New Russia, as it was then called, were mostly nomads and Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the sense accurately. Replace the Kiswahili phrase that renders "nomads" as "wavamizi" (invaders) with the correct word for nomads (e.g., “wahamaji wa kabila/waimami” or “wao walikuwa wahamaji/wanahamaji”), and render "Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia" as “Cossack, kundi la nusu-wahamaji lililopo tambarare za Urusi.” Preserve sentence structure and HTML tags.
findings.translation_quote: Wakazi wa New Russia, kama ilivyokuwa ikitajwa wakati huo, waliokuwa zaidi wavamizi wa maeneo na Cossacks, kundi la nusu-wahamaji lililokuwa katika tambarare za Urusi.

findings.location: Paragraph beginning "And so, they embraced the invading Germans."
findings.source_quote: And so, they embraced the invading Germans.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the mistranslation of "invading Germans." The Kiswahili currently uses “Wajerumani waliotovuliwa,” which falsely means "disrobed Germans" or is nonsensical. Replace with a correct translation such as “wakakumbatia Wajerumani waliovamia” or “walikumbatia Waarabu?" (use the correct ethnic name). Ensure the verb conveys "invading" (e.g., "waliovamia").

findings.source_quote: that was vehemently anti-Communist- to this beleaguered group of believers, this must have seemed to be a God sent miracle to deliver them from their burdensome exile.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the parenthetical/English phrase into Kiswahili rather than leaving an English term in parentheses. Replace “na ambayo ilikuwa kwa msimamo mkali dhidi ya Kialamu (Anti-Communist)” with a single fluent Kiswahili rendering such as “na ambayo ilikuwa dhidi ya Ukomunisti kwa msimamo mkali” or “iliyokuwa kwa msimamo mkali dhidi ya Ukomunisti.” Keep meaning and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: na ambayo ilikuwa kwa msimamo mkali dhidi ya Kialamu (Anti-Communist) — kwa kundi hili la waumini walioteseka, hili lilionekana kama muujiza...

findings.source_quote: “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established” (Proverbs 4:26).
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the Bible book name into conventional Kiswahili while keeping the chapter:verse numbers unchanged. Replace the English parenthetical reference “(Proverbs 4:26)” with the Kiswahili book name and the same numbers, e.g., “(Mithali 4:26).” The quoted proverb itself is already translated; ensure the book name is localized.
findings.translation_quote: “Tafakari njia za miguu yako, na yawe njia zako zote zimarishwe” (Proverbs 4:26).

findings.source_quote: the agricultural communities ... were collectivized and put under government control.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not leave the English term in parentheses. Replace “(collectivized)” with a Kiswahili equivalent (e.g., “kulikotwa umiliki wa pamoja” or “kulikokolezwa/kuunganishwa umiliki/kuwekwa katika mifumo ya umiliki wa pamoja”) and remove the English word, producing a fluent Kiswahili sentence.
findings.translation_quote: Ibada za kidini mara chache ziliruhusiwa, na jamii za kilimo ... zilikusanywa kanuni za umiliki wa pamoja (collectivized) na kuwekwa chini ya udhibiti wa serikali.
